rule.description: A trait violates interface segregation when it forces required methods onto every implementor that no client in the defining crate can exercise. One rule, two bands of the same required-and-unused measurement: (1) a fat interface with at least 8 required methods of which at least 3 are never called by any client outside the trait's own definition and implementations in the defining crate; (2) a small capability trait of at most 4 required methods whose entire interface is unused in the defining crate while that crate implements the trait, forcing the capability onto implementors.
rule.implementation: Dylint lint library (rustc late-lint pass, late_lint_mod via check_crate) driven through a vendored dylint_driver as RUSTC_WRAPPER over `cargo check --workspace --all-features`; usage is measured with HIR def-ids resolved through typeck results, and calls made inside the trait's own definition or own trait impls do not count as client usage.

detection_procedure: Discover the repository root (SMELL_CHECK_REPO, or walk up from the working directory to a Cargo workspace, or /workspace/repo).
Ensure the rustc-dev component is present so rustc_private is linkable; rustup installs it when missing.

Build the vendored Dylint driver and the fat_interface lint library into a machine-local cache, then run cargo check --workspace --all-features with the driver as RUSTC_WRAPPER, DYLINT_LIBS pointing at the built library, and DYLINT_NO_DEPS=1 so only workspace crates are linted.

Parse every `warning: fat_interface` block: report its location, trait name, and the structural evidence message. Zero matches exits 0, one or more matches exit 1 with the evidence printed, and an incomplete analysis (unbuildable tree, missing workspace, missing components) exits 2 without verdict.

fat-valt-core-contract.description: The core value trait is turned into a fat interface: the string/sequence/number capability methods (into_seq, is_int, as_isize, as_f64, is_utf8_str, as_bytes, as_sub_str, from_utf8_bytes) are hoisted from jaq_std::ValT into jaq_core::ValT as required methods. Every value type in the ecosystem must now implement them, while clients of the defining crate jaq-core still exercise none of the 8 hoisted methods there.
fat-valt-core-contract.expected_repair: Split the merged trait back along the capability boundary its clients rely on: keep the small core contract in jaq-core and move the JSON-oriented capability surface into a separate trait that only value types with those capabilities implement.

hasinputs-capability-payload.description: The optional input-stream capability is turned into mandatory payload: trait HasInputs moves to the core crate, becomes a bound on the associated Data type of the core DataT contract, and the core crate itself implements it only via a leak-stub that yields an empty stream. Nothing in the defining crate ever calls inputs(); the capability is dead weight that every data kind must now carry.
hasinputs-capability-payload.expected_repair: Make the capability opt-in again: keep HasInputs as a separate interface a data kind can implement, and let the inputs filters demand it only through a where clause on the data type instead of a mandatory associated-type bound.

checks.description: Band 1 of rule fat_interface: a trait with >= 8 required methods of which >= 3 are never called by any client in the defining crate.

matches.evidence: trait `ValT` forces 19 required methods onto every implementor, but 8 of them are never used by any client in the defining crate (into_seq, is_int, as_isize, as_f64, is_utf8_str, as_bytes, as_sub_str, from_utf8_bytes); split the interface along the capability boundaries its clients actually rely on

checks.description: Band 2 of rule fat_interface: a trait of 1..=4 required methods whose entire interface is unused in the defining crate while that crate implements it.

matches.evidence: capability trait `HasInputs` is implemented in the defining crate, yet its entire interface (inputs) is never called there; keep the interface opt-in so implementors are not forced to carry unused capability
